public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 428

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/428](https://www.erdosproblems.com/428)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Set

namespace Erdos428

/--
The density ratio of set $A$ up to $n$ relative to the prime counting function $\pi(n)$.
-/
noncomputable def primeDensityRatio (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (A ∩ Icc 1 n).ncard / (primeCounting n)

/--
Is there a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that, for infinitely many $n$, all of $n-a$
are prime for all $a\in A$ with $0 < a < n$ and $$\liminf\frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\pi(x)}>0?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_428 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      (∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a → a < n → (n - a).Prime) ∧
      liminf (fun n ↦ primeDensityRatio A n) atTop > 0 := by
  sorry

end Erdos428

review.notes: No mathematical defect was identified in the Lean semantics, but source fidelity remains unverified. Scratch proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish that every admissible n satisfies |A ∩ [1,n]| ≤ π(n)+1 and primeDensityRatio A n ≤ 2. Consequently, infinitely many admissible n make the set of eventual lower bounds bounded above; it is also nonempty since the ratio is nonnegative. A compiled equivalence proves that the stated positive real liminf is exactly the existence of an eventual positive constant lower bound. Thus the real-valued liminf does not introduce an infinity/default-value defect here. Additional compiled checks establish that finite A have liminf zero and that removing 0 changes neither condition. The numerator is always the cardinality of a finite set, division is real-valued, and the zero denominators at n=0,1 affect only initial terms. The accessible community database records 428 as open, consistent with the category.
